nodes.question: Can the source mug be reliably matched to an edited object, and what visible continuity cues support that match?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visible identity or continuity evidence reliably links the source mug to a specific edited object and permits its position to be judged. Fail only if clear evidence establishes that no matching source mug is present. Unknown if the blue blur, changed appearance, multiple mugs, or other ambiguity prevents a reliable match. Report the source mug's distinctive shape, handle, color, and scale against each plausible edited object; do not treat mere scene continuity or a plausible location as a match.
nodes.binding: Compare the source's large light-blue handled mug left of the headphones with the edited scene. Assess the blue blurred remnant and each pale mug separately, including the mug right of the headphones. State the specific matching cues and limitations; do not assume either pale mug is the source mug.

nodes.question: Using the source-mug identity evidence, is the same mug to the right of the headphones, or is there clear evidence of movement toward that right-side relation without completion?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the same source mug is reliably identified and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Fail only if the same mug is reliably identified and clear comparison shows no movement toward the right-side relation; report its source and edited positions. Unknown if identity or displacement cannot be resolved. Movement toward the right-side relation without reaching it is evidence of partial progress only when the same mug and that displacement are established; movement in another direction, a different mug on the right, or object presence alone is not progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1's specific identity/continuity observations, then compare the tracked mug's source and edited positions relative to the headphones. Explicitly report identity cues, displacement direction, and whether the right-side relation is achieved. Do not infer movement from the other mugs or the blue blur alone.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using only the saved support observations. Complete (yes) only if s1 and s2 establish that the source mug itself is identified in the edit and is visibly to the right of the headphones. Partial only if s2 records evidence that this same mug moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right. Absent (no) only if the observations provide clear evidence that no requested movement progressed. Unknown if source-mug identity, movement, or position is unresolved, or if the observations do not establish progress or absence. A different mug's position, object presence, or unrelated edits cannot establish fulfillment.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s2: The node’s binding is truncated/underspecified (“(...)”), and its repeated traces all return unknown despite strong visible evidence of an edit. Repair the binding so it explicitly consumes s1’s identity/continuity findings and compares the source mug’s position with each plausible edited continuation, rather than treating imperfect identity matching as an automatic stop. In these images, the original large light-blue mug is left of the headphones; the edit has a blue blur at the former left position, a small mug near the headphones, and another mug to their right. This supports possible movement/progress, but does not by itself prove which edited object is the same mug. Require the node to weigh continuity cues (color, shape, handle, scale, location) and report the evidence and uncertainty; distinguish a plausible partial displacement from a confirmed completed move, and do not count an unrelated mug or blur alone as progress. The five high-confidence unknown traces are repeated variation, not independent evidence that identity or displacement is impossible; investigate whether s1’s observations are actually available and whether the binding routes them correctly. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport/schema failure. Preserve unresolved when evidence truly cannot establish continuity, but avoid making exact identity certainty a prerequisite for considering convergent visual evidence of partial progress; the reference label constrains the aggregate, not the atomic identity judgment.
s1: The binding is truncated and does not clearly route the node’s own identity/continuity observations into the decision. Make the structural edit explicit: compare the source mug against the left blue remnant and both edited mugs individually, recording color, body shape, handle, relative scale, and position, then assess whether the combined evidence supports continuity and movement. Here the source is a large light-blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blue blur at that location, a small pale mug near the headphones, and a pale handled mug to their right. The right mug’s location is consistent with the requested destination, but its changed appearance and the other plausible objects leave identity uncertain; do not treat location alone as proof or let imperfect identity automatically erase evidence of possible partial progress. Distinguish plausible progress from a confirmed completed move, and retain unresolved when the visual evidence genuinely cannot support a judgment. The repeated high-confidence unknowns are not independent evidence of impossibility. Traces are valid and queried with no dependency or transport failures, so focus on binding, evidence routing, and the criterion’s handling of uncertainty—not schema repair or forcing the aggregate label.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not preserve the requested relation and extent reliably. s2 treats movement “toward” the right as partial even though the instruction only requests the final relation “to the right”; movement toward it could be in an unrelated direction or leave the mug still left of the headphones. Conversely, s2’s fail condition (“did not move toward”) does not establish that no requested progress occurred, so it cannot support absence. The fulfillment readout inherits this unsupported partial/absent logic. Require evidence of movement toward the right-side relation for partial, and clear evidence of no such progress for absent; otherwise leave unresolved.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The program adds an unsupported mandatory identity-tracking condition: the instruction asks that the mug be to the right of the headphones, but does not require proving it is the same source mug or proving movement from its original position. This can leave fulfillment unresolved even when the requested final relation is visibly satisfied. The support checks also make progress depend on tracking that same mug, so they can miss valid requested progress. The saved readout otherwise follows the rubric’s complete/partial/absent/unknown distinctions.

The support checks do not reliably establish the requested change. s1 observes only the edited image’s final layout, while s2’s criteria require evidence of progress toward the relation and its binding asks for a source-versus-edited comparison that the saved question does not explicitly require. More importantly, s2 treats any mug to the right as pass, and fulfillment treats that as completion, although the instruction requests moving the mug; a final right-side mug alone does not establish that the requested edit occurred. The readout therefore can overclaim completion and cannot consistently distinguish no progress from partial progress.
